tasks.title: Temperature: the fahrenheit property
tasks.statement: Add a fahrenheit property to Temperature: reading gives degrees Fahrenheit by the formula C * 9 / 5 + 32, and writing converts back and stores the value in celsius.
tasks.hint: @property def fahrenheit(self); @fahrenheit.setter def fahrenheit(self, value): self.celsius = (value - 32) * 5 / 9.

tasks.title: Age with validation
tasks.statement: Turn age into a property: the value must be an integer and non-negative, otherwise ValueError. The check must work both when the object is created (in __init__ assign via self.age) and on later assignment.
tasks.hint: Store the number in self._age; in the setter: if not isinstance(value, int) or value < 0: raise ValueError.

tasks.title: Read-only
tasks.statement: Add computed properties area and perimeter to Rect without setters: they are always recomputed from w and h, and trying to assign to area raises AttributeError.

tasks.title: The Positive descriptor
tasks.statement: Write a data descriptor Positive: the value must be a positive number, otherwise ValueError. Store it in the instance under the field name (__set_name__ will give it) so values of different objects do not get mixed; when accessed through the class, return the descriptor itself.
tasks.hint: __set_name__(self, owner, name): self.name = name; __set__: obj.__dict__[self.name] = value; __get__: if obj is None: return self.

tasks.title: The Typed descriptor
tasks.statement: Write a data descriptor Typed(expected_type): on assignment it checks isinstance and raises TypeError if the type is wrong. Values are stored in the instances (in obj.__dict__ under the field name).
tasks.hint: In __set__: if not isinstance(value, self.expected_type): raise TypeError(...). __get__: return obj.__dict__[self.name].

tasks.title: A lazy attribute
tasks.statement: Write a non-data descriptor lazy (used as a decorator): on first access it calls the function, puts the result into obj.__dict__ under the same name and returns it, and afterwards the function never runs. When accessed through the class, return the descriptor itself.
tasks.hint: __set_name__ remembers the name; in __get__: value = self.func(obj); obj.__dict__[self.name] = value; return value. There must be no __set__ method.

tasks.title: Your own classmethod
tasks.statement: Write a descriptor MyClassMethod, a simplified classmethod. In __get__ it returns a bound method with the class passed first (the one through which it was accessed, even if called via a subclass or an instance).
tasks.hint: def __get__(self, obj, owner=None): if owner is None: owner = type(obj); return types.MethodType(self.func, owner).

tasks.title: Slots for Point
tasks.statement: Add a __slots__ attribute with the fields x and y to Point, so that instances have no __dict__ and new attributes cannot be added.

tasks.title: Caching a heavy sum
tasks.statement: Report.total computes the sum of the values on every access (the calls counter grows). Make the sum computed once per instance, without changing the call r.total.
tasks.hint: from functools import cached_property and replace @property with @cached_property.
